bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar extends student credit card scheme till 2030-31, loans up to Rs 4 lakh: Check how to apply
bihar_raw_news.content: The Bihar government has extended the Student Credit Card Scheme for another five years to help more students continue their higher education. The scheme will now remain in operation until the financial year 2030-31. Along with the extension, the government has introduced a new framework aimed at making the scheme easier to access and more financially sustainable. Students will continue to be eligible for education loans of up to Rs 4 lakh under the scheme. The state government has also approved Rs 950 crore for the current financial year to provide education loans. Advertisement So far, around 4.15 lakh students in Bihar have received financial support for higher education through the scheme. The extension is expected to help more students who may otherwise struggle to pay for their studies. Advertisement What is the Bihar Student Credit Card Scheme? The Bihar Student Credit Card Scheme was introduced by the Department of Education to provide financial support to students who want to pursue higher education but face financial difficulties. Under the scheme, eligible students can get education loans of up to Rs 4 lakh at a low interest rate. The money can be used to pay for higher education courses such as B.Sc, B.A, B.Tech and MBBS, among others. बिहार स्टूडेंट क्रेडिट कार्ड योजना में खर्च की स्वीकृति बढ़ी। अगले पांच वर्षों के लिए योजना का किया गया विस्तार। #BiharHigherEducationDept pic.twitter.com/TL1KuBo6mS — Education Department, Bihar (@BiharEducation_) September 7, 2026 To be eligible, the applicant must be a resident of Bihar and should have passed Class 12. The student must also be admitted to a recognised course at an authorised institution and complete the course. The applicant must be at least 25 years old. How to Apply and What Documents Are Needed? Visit https://www.7nishchay-yuvaupmission.bihar.gov.in/ website and click the ‘New Applicant Registration’ button. Applicants must enter details such as their name, email ID, mobile number and Aadhaar number and complete the OTP verification. After registration, the username and password are sent through email and SMS. The applicant then needs to log in, complete the Personal Information section and select BSCC from the available options. After filling in and submitting the BSCC application form, an acknowledgement number is generated. The District Registration and Counseling Center (DRCC) will then provide an appointment date through SMS and email. The applicant must visit the DRCC with self-attested documents for verification. Once the documents are verified and the loan is approved by the bank, the applicant will be informed about when to collect the Student Credit Card and loan sanction letter. After collecting these documents, the student has to visit the bank and complete the required paperwork. The bank will then disburse the approved loan. bihar_raw_news.title: 'Resolving people's problems and ensuring justice is our duty': Bihar CM - ANI News
bihar_raw_news.content: ‘Resolving people’s problems and ensuring justice is our duty’: Bihar CM ANI | Updated: Sep 08, 2026 15:58 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel Patna (Bihar) [India], September 8 (ANI): Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary on Tuesday said that resolving the grievances of citizens and ensuring justice is the government’s responsibility, asserting that the ‘Sahyog Programme’ has emerged as an important mechanism for addressing public concerns. A total of 137 applicants attended the state-level Sahyog Programme at the Chief Minister’s Secretariat in Patna. Their grievances were heard, and directions were issued to the concerned departments and district administrations for time-bound action. Choudhary directed officials to address public grievances with transparency, sensitivity and within the prescribed timeframe, saying that the confidence people have placed in the Sahyog Programme must be strengthened and sustained. Applicants from different parts of Bihar raised issues concerning the Revenue and Land Reforms, Education, Home, Rural Works, Health, Food and Consumer Protection, Social Welfare and other departments. The Chief Minister directed the concerned District Magistrates and departmental officials to ensure that the cases are resolved within the stipulated period. The concerned departments and district administrations assured the applicants that necessary action would be taken at the earliest. "Applicants whose grievances have already been resolved need not travel to Patna to attend the state-level programme. However, those facing complex cases that remain unresolved at the district level can approach the state-level Sahyog Programme for further redressal", CM said. "The government is committed to ensuring a transparent, impartial and time-bound resolution of citizens’ grievances. The state-level programme provides a mechanism to review complex cases and facilitate just and speedy decisions", CM said, The Chief Minister also directed officials to ensure that eligible beneficiaries receive old-age pensions and ration cards without delay. He stressed that no eligible person should be denied the benefits of government welfare schemes because of technical issues. He said the government aims to resolve grievances received through Sahyog camps within 30 days, and directed officials and employees to work with complete transparency and sensitivity while ensuring satisfactory disposal of cases. Senior officials, including Chief Minister’s Principal Secretary Deepak Kumar, Chief Secretary Pratyay Amrit, Director General of Police Vinay Kumar, Chief Minister’s Secretary Lokesh Kumar Singh and Chief Minister’s Secretary Sanjay Kumar Singh, along with senior officials of various departments, attended the programme. District Magistrates, Senior Superintendents of Police/Superintendents of Police and other senior officials from across Bihar participated in the programme through video conferencing. (ANI)

bihar_raw_news.content: News On AIR | September 8, 2026 1:33 PM Bihar makes an impressive investment pitch at AIM Congress in Dubai A delegation led by Bihar Industries Minister Ms Shreyasi Singh is participating in the Annual Investment Meeting (AIM) Congress being held in Dubai from 7th to 9th September. Yesterday, the state made an impactful presentation at the event, pitching Bihar’s investment opportunities and highlighting sectors with potential for investors. Bihar stressed the strength of existing people-to-people connections, growing infrastructure and its immense human resources to attract international investments to boost industrial development, infrastructure and employment generation. The investors were informed about the seamless road connectivity, surplus power supply and extraordinary achievements in the field of enabling infrastructure as well as government policies. The Minister also took a Q&A session with the participating potential investors and answered a range of queries on the possibilities offered by the state. Addressing the gathering, Ms. Singh said that Bihar is now moving beyond its glorious past and writing a new story of development and industrial growth. She highlighted Bihar’s improved road connectivity and changing image, saying this reflects the growing confidence and self-belief in the state. She invited investors to partner with Bihar and become part of its journey towards a developed and prosperous state.

The Bureau of Energy Efficiency, under the Ministry of Power, received formal confirmation that the CCTS meets the criteria under the Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism Regulations 2026. Carbon Credit Trading Scheme The Carbon Credit Trading Scheme is India’s market-based mechanism for reducing greenhouse gas emissions through tradable carbon credits. The scheme is linked to domestic carbon pricing and can be used by exporters to show that a carbon cost has already been paid in India. Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism The Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism is a border tax framework used to align the carbon cost of imported goods with the carbon cost faced by domestic producers. The UK CBAM is scheduled to begin on 1 January 2027 and applies to carbon-intensive imports. Trade Relief and Covered Goods Under the UK mechanism, importers of Indian goods can claim relief on CBAM liability for the effective carbon price already paid in India. bihar_raw_news.content: News Facebook Twitter WhatsApp Linkedin Copy URL The Bihar government has announced plans to establish a dedicated Teacher Training University aimed at strengthening the skills and capacity of educators across the state. Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary made the announcement on Teachers’ Day, highlighting the need for continuous professional development for teachers. The proposed university will provide regular training to teachers working across different levels of education, from primary schools to higher education, engineering and polytechnic institutions. Bihar currently has more than seven lakh teachers, making large-scale capacity building a key focus of the initiative. Alongside the university, Bihar is planning to develop a modern AI ecosystem in collaboration with Microsoft, Google and Sarvam AI. Under this initiative, teachers will receive training in emerging AI technologies and tools to support more effective teaching and learning. The state has also finalised an MoU with Google specifically for AI-focused teacher training. Also Read: Odisha launches ‘AI Course for All’ to build future-ready skills The government is also exploring the establishment of a Banaras Hindu University (BHU) centre in Bihar, which could expand access to higher education opportunities for students within the state. The initiatives reflect Bihar’s broader push towards technology-enabled education, teacher development and modernisation of its education system. bihar_raw_news.title: Tejashwi Yadav urges Centre to declare Bihar floods a national disaster
bihar_raw_news.content: Tejashwi Yadav urges Centre to declare Bihar floods a national disaster RJD leader Tejashwi Yadav has urged Prime Minister Narendra Modi to declare Bihar’s floods a national disaster and provide Rs 5,000 crore in immediate assistance. He also sought enhanced rescue operations, farmer relief, an audit and a long-term flood resilience mission By IANS Published Date - 8 September 2026, 12:15 AM Patna: As severe floods continue to affect large parts of Bihar, Leader of the Opposition Tejashwi Yadav has written to Prime Minister Narendra Modi, urging the Centre to declare the situation a national disaster and provide immediate financial assistance of Rs 5,000 crore to the state. More than a dozen districts have been affected by the floods, with lakhs of people facing difficulties caused by rising river levels, damaged infrastructure and disrupted connectivity. In his letter, Yadav said the situation had affected 20 districts and caused extensive damage to life, property and public infrastructure. He said flood-affected people were struggling to access basic necessities, including food, clean drinking water, medicines, electricity, cattle fodder and safe transportation. Yadav criticised the relief and rescue measures being undertaken by the Bihar government and the NDA-led Centre, describing the assistance as inadequate considering the scale of the crisis. He also accused the Bihar government and NDA leaders from the state of failing to secure adequate central assistance and a national-disaster declaration. The RJD leader argued that Bihar’s recurring floods are not solely a natural disaster but also reflect years of inadequate disaster preparedness, mitigation and adaptation. He pointed out that despite floods occurring almost every year, sufficient measures for a permanent solution have not been implemented. Yadav also raised questions over the state government’s financial preparedness for the crisis. He alleged that Bihar’s Contingency Fund and other financial resources had been diverted towards routine government expenditure, leaving insufficient funds for flood relief. The RJD leader called for an independent review or CAG audit of the state’s financial and disaster-management preparedness and the utilisation of the State Contingency Fund. In his letter, Yadav urged the Prime Minister and the Central Government to take immediate measures, including declare the devastating floods in Bihar a national disaster, provide Rs 5,000 crore in immediate financial assistance along with a special flood-relief package, deploy additional boats and other resources to flood-hit areas where road connectivity has been disrupted, deploy the Army and Air Force wherever necessary for rescue and relief operations and ensure assistance through helicopters, ensure adequate supplies of food, drinking water, medicines, animal fodder and temporary shelters, provide special financial assistance to farmers, labourers, livestock owners and affected families, and conduct an independent review or CAG audit of the state’s disaster-management preparedness and the utilisation and transactions of the State Contingency Fund. Yadav also called for a comprehensive, long-term Flood Resilience Mission to address Bihar’s recurring flood crisis. According to him, the mission should focus on river and embankment management, drainage systems, rejuvenation of water bodies, modern flood forecasting and improved water-management policies. national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi today inaugurated and laid the foundation stones for various development initiatives worth over ₹35,000 crore in Vadodara. The PM dedicated to the nation three key sections of the Western Dedicated Freight Corridor, marking the full completion and operationalisation of the Freight Corridor network. Addressing the huge gathering, Prime Minister Modi highlighted the rapid transformation of India’s transport and logistics sector, calling the completion of over 2,800 kilometres of Dedicated Freight Corridors a historic achievement for 21st-century India and a testament to the nation’s changing work culture. The Prime Minister pointed out that although the project was initially conceived in 2006, it suffered from years of inaction. Contrastingly, the accelerated execution over the past decade has completely transformed the national logistics ecosystem, which serves as a lifeline for the rapidly developing India. Emphasising the operational impact, the Prime Minister noted that separating freight traffic from passenger lines has drastically improved efficiency. He underlined that this massive reduction in travel time is driving substantial fuel savings, lowering environmental impact, and establishing a faster, cleaner supply chain for the entire nation. Mr Modi also added that India’s youth are witnessing government thrust across solar, nuclear, and wind energy sectors. Emphasising the future of technology, the Prime Minister remarked that as upcoming industries, including artificial intelligence, will be entirely power-driven, the government is focussing on establishing a robust, multi-sectoral energy ecosystem to power India’s future growth. The Prime Minister emphasised that India has emerged as a global manufacturing hub, now producing its own advanced train and metro coaches. He noted that over 50 thousand modern railway coaches and two point five lakh wagons have been added to the Indian Railways network. Outlining the vision of “Chip to Ship” local production, he stated that a complete, self-reliant supply chain is being forged within the country, spanning high-tech electronics to heavy maritime shipping. During the programme, the Prime Minister also flagged off freight train services from New Sanand, New Makarpura, New Umbergaon, and New JNPT, along with a new passenger train service between Tanda Road and Vadodara, connecting remote tribal regions of Alirajpur to the national rail grid. Mr Modi also laid the foundation stone for three railway expansion projects worth over ₹9,700 crore and three National Highway projects costing around ₹1,780 crore to ease congestion and boost connectivity across Gujarat and Madhya Pradesh. He also launched various civic and infrastructure projects of the Gujarat Government worth ₹2,600 crore, including megawatt floating solar plant at Kadana Dam and PMAY housing units. Later, the PM will also visit Navsari to inaugurate the BJP’s new AI-enabled, high-tech office in Navsari.

national_raw_news.title: 6 hours ago | National 463 DAC clears acquisition proposals worth over Rs 1.10 lakh cr for Forces
national_raw_news.content: The Defence Acquisition Council (DAC) today cleared capital acquisition proposals worth over 1.10 lakh crore rupees for the defence forces. The approval was granted during a meeting of the Council held under the Chairmanship of Defence Minister Rajnath Singh. The proposals include, procurement of Chemical Biological Radiological and Nuclear (CBRN) Recce Vehicles, High Mobility Vehicles (HMV), Self-Propelled Mechanical Mine Layers (MML), Advanced Light Helicopters (ALHs), Trawl Tanks and Sarvatra Bridge System for the Indian Army. For the Indian Navy, Acceptance of Necessity was accorded for the procurement of Arudhra Radars, Design and Development and subsequent procurement of Marine Gas Turbines (MGT). Arudhra Radar will replace the existing Air Route Surveillance Radars at various Naval Air Stations and MGT, a warship propulsion system, will reduce dependency on foreign vendors. Meanwhile, for the Indian Air Force, approval was granted to various proposals to enhance the war-fighting capability of fighters, transports and helicopters. Approval was also accorded for procuring Ground-Based Multi-Purpose Jammer (GBMPJ) and installing Defence Forces Secure Access Card (DEFSAC) System. Defence Ministry said that 98 percent of total procurements will be made from the Indian Industry. The CBRN Recce Vehicles will be capable of detecting, identifying, monitoring and marking of areas contaminated with CBRN agents. The HMVs will enhance operational capabilities, logistic support and mobility in challenging terrains. The MMLs will achieve the desired operational capability in terms of fast and responsive minelaying in difficult terrains. The ALHs will execute complex missions across all terrains and operational situations for the Indian Army and the Indian Air Force. The Trawl Tanks and Bridge System will be utilised to provide composite crossings to fighting formations during operations in varied terrains. The GBMPJ will provide effective jamming against radars of adversaries and DEFSAC will replace existing paper based Identity Card, Passes, Permits with an interoperable Radio Frequency Identification-based smart cards system.

national_raw_news.title: 6 hours ago | National 296 India joins 24 countries in global initiative on 6G technology
national_raw_news.content: India has joined the United States and 24 other countries in an international initiative aimed at shaping the development of next-generation 6G networks. In a social media post, the US Department of Commerce said, India had joined the US and 24 other countries in an effort to ensure that next-generation networks reflect shared security interests, strengthen competitiveness and drive innovation. The announcement came after Union Minister of State for Commerce and Industry Jitin Prasada met US Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick on the sidelines of the G20 Innovation Ministerial. The two leaders discussed the future of 6G technology and the importance of international cooperation in developing next-generation telecommunications networks. During the meeting, India and the US discussed strengthening cooperation in semiconductors, AI and data centres. MoS Prasada encouraged the possibility of more US investments in ISM 2.0, proposed strengthening AI technology partnership and shared a mechanism for safeguards for AI. Jitin Prasada led the Indian delegation at the G20 Innovation Minister’s meeting held on September 1 and September 2 in Chapel Hill, North Carolina, United States, hosted by the US Department of Commerce and the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy (OSTP). The meeting concluded with the G20 Innovation Ministerial Statement, highlighting the potential of emerging technologies to drive prosperity, productivity and opportunity. India reaffirmed its commitment to building strategic partnerships in AI, semiconductors, DPI, robotics and other emerging technologies into greater opportunities for innovation, economic growth and an improved quality of life for its citizens.

national_raw_news.title: International Literacy Day observed today with focus on literacy for people, planet and prosperity
national_raw_news.content: Today is International Literacy Day. The Day is celebrated on the 8th of September every year to remind everyone of the importance of literacy for individuals, communities and societies. This year the theme for International Literacy Day is “Literacy for people, the planet and prosperity”. Proclaimed by UNESCO in 1966 during the 14th session of its General Conference, International Literacy Day provides an opportunity to review progress, deepen understanding of persistent and emerging challenges, and shape future literacy agendas in a rapidly changing world. To mark the International Literacy Day 2026, UNESCO, in collaboration with the Government of Mexico, is organising a global celebration on “Literacy for People, the Planet and Prosperity” in Mexico. The event will also feature the presentation of the UNESCO International Literacy Prizes. The main objectives of the global conference include taking stock of literacy progress since 2015 and its contribution to sustainable development and peace; to celebrate progress achieved in Mexico and in Latin America and the Caribbean; to identify effective policies, as well as approaches and solutions for literacy provision, practice and monitoring across lifelong learning ecosystems; and to discuss the draft Action Plan for the implementation of the UNESCO Global Alliance for Literacy Strategy (2026-2029) among others. Literacy is a fundamental human right for all. It opens the door to the enjoyment of other human rights, greater freedoms, and global citizenship.

Bookmark stories for easy access on any device or the Swarajya app . Sign In Prefer Prefer PM Modi (Pic Via PIB) A security scare unfolded at the Mumbai venue where Prime Minister Narendra Modi is due to appear, after city police picked up two men, one of them carrying a firearm and the other found with forged Prime Minister's Office identity papers, NDTV reported . Sources said the pair was taken into custody late on Monday night (7 September) while a security protocol drill was under way. Police said a gun was seized from one of them. According to police, a man was spotted behaving suspiciously at the Nita Mukesh Ambani Cultural Centre in the Bandra Kurla Complex, the site of the Prime Minister's programme. He was detained along with his bodyguard, who was in possession of the weapon. The man, identified as 24-year-old Rohan Parekh, told officers he worked for the PMO, but verification revealed that the identity card he was carrying was fake. "Three men allegedly used a suspicious government ID card and forced their way, armed with a firearm, past mall security into Jio World Plaza, BKC," the police said in a statement, adding that an FIR has been filed. "The weapon has been found to be licensed and two persons are arrested in this regard," the police said, stressing that the episode occurred on Monday and bears no link to the Prime Minister's engagement on Tuesday (8 September). The episode nevertheless prompted heightened vigilance ahead of Modi's arrival. Officers are questioning the two men to establish why they entered the premises armed and with fabricated credentials. Given the gravity of the matter, the Mumbai Crime Branch has assumed charge of the probe. The Prime Minister is scheduled to open Global Fintech Fest 2026 at the venue on Tuesday evening. The four-day gathering, among the largest fintech conferences anywhere, carries the theme "Potential to Impact: Agentic AI, Tokenisation, Quantum - Trusted, Connected, Global Systems for Inclusive Finance." national_raw_news.title: PM-SETU approves Rs 735.70 crore plans for ITI clusters in Rajasthan, UP, Telangana
national_raw_news.content: PM-SETU approves Rs 735.70 crore plans for ITI clusters in Rajasthan, UP, Telangana Toggle navigation हिंदी खबर PM-SETU approves Rs 735.70 crore plans for ITI clusters in Rajasthan, UP, Telangana ANI | Updated: Sep 08, 2026 14:28 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], September 8 (ANI): The National Steering Committee under the Pradhan Mantri Skilling and Employability Transformation through Upgraded ITIs (PM-SETU) has approved Strategic Investment Plans worth Rs 735.70 crore for three ITI clusters in Rajasthan , Uttar Pradesh and Telangana , taking the scheme's total sanctioned investment to Rs 2,171 crore across nine ITI clusters. The approvals are aimed at accelerating the transformation of government Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs) through an industry-led approach, with investments in infrastructure, new courses and training programmes aligned with evolving industry requirements, the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship said in a release. The 5th National Steering Committee meeting, chaired by MSDE Secretary Debashree Mukherjee, approved Rs 241 crore for the Bhiwadi ITI cluster in Rajasthan , Rs 254.30 crore for the Medchal cluster in Telangana and Rs 240.40 crore for the Meerut cluster in Uttar Pradesh. In Rajasthan , H.G. Infra Engineering's plan covers five ITIs, with Government ITI Bhiwadi as the main institute. In Telangana , ZEN Technologies' plan covers five ITIs, with Government ITI Medchal as the main institute. The Telangana plan was earlier deferred for clarifications on operational and financial aspects. In Uttar Pradesh, the National Skill Development Corporation's plan covers five ITIs under the Meerut cluster, with Government ITI, Saket, Meerut as the main institute. The approved plans provide for infrastructure modernisation, upgrading existing trades, introducing new long-term and short-term courses and strengthening operational capabilities, the ministry said. A key implementation milestone was also recorded with the signing of a Shareholders' Agreement among H.G. Infra Engineering, the Rajasthan government and MSDE for the Bhiwadi cluster. Rajasthan has become the first state to execute an SHA under PM-SETU, marking the formal commencement of implementation activities for the cluster. The ministry said the PM-SETU cluster-based model is intended to strengthen ITIs' capacity to provide skills aligned with emerging technologies, changing industry requirements and evolving employment opportunities. national_raw_news.title: Arunachal media delegation explores Gujarat's development journey, heritage and infrastructure
national_raw_news.content: Echo Of Arunachal Newsflash State News Arunachal media delegation explores Gujarat’s development journey, heritage and infrastructure Ahmedabad, Sep 7: A nine-member media delegation from Arunachal Pradesh began its seven-day press tour of Gujarat on Monday, visiting key institutions and projects showcasing the State’s development in governance, urban planning, heritage and transport infrastructure. The tour commenced at the Press Information Bureau (PIB), Ahmedabad, where the delegation was welcomed by Additional Director General Siddhartha Bodke. Interacting with the visiting journalists, Bodke briefed them on PIB’s role in disseminating information on government policies, programmes and initiatives and encouraged the media team to make the most of the field visits and expert interactions lined up during the tour. The delegation next visited Kochrab Ashram, Mahatma Gandhi's first ashram established after returning from South Africa in 1915, where the journalists interacted with Dr Prasana Gandhi, who briefed them on the historical and cultural significance of the Ashram and its association with the Father of the Nation, his philosophy and India’s freedom movement. The journalists also undertook a cruise on the Sabarmati River, observing the riverfront development and the surrounding urban landscape. The visit provided an opportunity to understand Ahmedabad’s riverfront transformation and its integration with the city’s urban development. At Centre for Environmental Planning and Technology (CEPT) University, the delegation interacted with President Barjor Mehta and senior faculty members on architecture, urban planning, education and research. The interaction also covered the institution’s contribution to shaping urban environments through education and research. The first day concluded with a visit to the Sabarmati Multimodal Transport Hub, where the delegation was briefed on the Mumbai-Ahmedabad High-Speed Rail (MAHSR) project. The interaction covered the scale and technical complexity of India’s first high-speed rail corridor, including engineering, planning, inter-agency coordination and on-ground execution. During the visit, Joint Director, PIB Itanagar, Utsav Parmar, also called on Principal Chief Project Manager Rajesh Agarwal. The seven-day press tour will take the Arunachal media delegation to several key sites and institutions across Gujarat, covering infrastructure, industry, technology, education, heritage and culture. The tour is aimed at providing the journalists with direct field exposure to major development initiatives and projects shaping Gujarat, enabling them to gain a broader understanding of the State’s development experience and its relevance to the diverse development landscape of the country. national_raw_news.title: US: MoS Jitin Prasada participates in G20 Innovation Ministers' meeting in Chapel Hill
national_raw_news.content: US: MoS Jitin Prasada participates in G20 Innovation Ministers’ meeting in Chapel Hill Toggle navigation हिंदी खबर US: MoS Jitin Prasada participates in G20 Innovation Ministers’ meeting in Chapel Hill ANI | Updated: Sep 07, 2026 22:00 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel North Carolina [US], September 7 (ANI): The Union Minister of State (MoS) Jitin Prasada led the Indian delegation at the G20 Innovation Ministers’ meeting held on September 1 and September 2 in Chapel Hill, North Carolina, United States (US), hosted by the US Department of Commerce and the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy (OSTP). According to the Ministry of Electronics and IT, the MoS was accompanied by Ajit Kumar, Joint Secretary, Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), senior officials from MeitY, Department of Science and Technology (DST) and Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT), as well as officials of the Embassy of India in the US. At the conclusion of the Ministerial, the G20 Ministers released the Innovation Ministerial Statement recognising that “emerging technologies have the potential to unlock prosperity, enhance productivity, and expand opportunity for all our peoples.” The consensus statement articulates shared broad agreement across six pillars, pro-innovation policy frameworks, technology for opportunity and prosperity, skilled technical workforce development, intellectual property policies for artificial intelligence (AI), AI for standards and standards for AI, and industrial innovation and investment in supply chains. Ministers also reached consensus on the Carolina Principles for Emerging Technologies, which call on countries to invest in foundational research, strengthen commercialisation pathways, and enable trusted technology adoption and deployment. Other deliverables of the Ministerial included the AI Prosperity Objectives and the AI Prosperity Compact, which will further technical workforce development across G20 nations and expand opportunities for private sector partnership. On the sidelines of the G20 Ministerial, Prasada held several bilateral discussions. In his bilateral meeting with Henna Virkkunen, Executive Vice-President of the European Commission, both discussed the importance of strengthening cooperation in innovation and building trusted digital ecosystems that enable technology-led growth and shared prosperity. In the meeting with Anne Le Hénanff, Minister Delegate for Artificial Intelligence and Digital Affairs of France, both sides discussed advancing cooperation in AI and digital technologies. India and France remain committed to strengthening technology-driven innovation and building partnerships for a trusted digital future, the Ministry said. During the meeting with Thomas Jarzombek and Silke Launert, Parliamentary State Secretaries, Germany, MoS explored opportunities to further deepen India–Germany collaboration in technology, innovation and research, driving shared progress and future-ready partnerships. In discussions with Prof Gaspard Banyankimbona, Commissioner for Education, Science, Technology and Innovation, African Union, the commitment to deepening partnership with Africa and creating new opportunities for shared growth and prosperity was highlighted by offering India Stack digital solutions, including DPI, to African countries. In the bilateral discussion with Howard Lutnick, US Secretary of Commerce, both sides exchanged views on strengthening cooperation across Semiconductors, AI and Data Centres. national_raw_news.content: Ministry of Finance Union Finance Minister meets delegation of bank employees representing different Public Sector Banks (PSBs) Scheme of Performance Linked Incentives (PLI) to Executives of Public Sector Banks kept in abeyance in response to Employees’ concerns Posted On: 07 SEP 2026 9:05PM by PIB Delhi The Union Finance Minister today met with a delegation of bank employees representing different Public Sector Banks (PSBs) led by the Bharatiya Mazdoor Sangh. The delegation raised various issues relating to the banking sector including review of ex-gratia, medical facility for retired employees, revisiting the present structure of Performance Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme applicable for the employees of PSBs, and other concerns related to employees. The concerns expressed by bank employees were taken cognizance of, and in response to the representation received on the PLI structure, it was decided to keep in abeyance the implementation of the PLI Scheme dated 19.11.2024 for FY 2025–26 and take up the same during the ongoing Bipartite Settlement/ Joint Note discussions. Salman’s briefing is understood to have covered the functioning of PIB in the region, giving the delegation an institutional grounding before they proceed to visit specific project sites and locations over the remainder of the week. Later on the first day, the delegation travelled to Gulmarg, the well known hill station in Baramulla district, where members experienced the region’s natural landscape and scenic beauty firsthand. The choice of Gulmarg as an early stop reflects both its standing as one of Kashmir’s most recognisable destinations and its symbolic value in showcasing the valley’s tourism appeal to visiting journalists who may go on to write about the region for audiences back home in Kerala.
